memory_candidates.content: When a foreground Bash call's command genuinely needs more than ~120s (e.g. a repo-wide verify-touched.sh/run-all.sh pass over 60+ suites), an inner `timeout N` wrapper on the command does NOT prevent the harness's own Bash tool from auto-backgrounding the call at its default ~120s ceiling. The fix is to raise the Bash tool's own `timeout` parameter (up to 600000ms) on that call, not just the inner shell timeout. Once a call has already been auto-backgrounded, recover by polling its output file directly (grep for a completion marker in a bounded loop) rather than idly waiting for the harness notification or re-running the command.

Decision pattern for a generated-surface-appending stage (plan-file-scope-harvest.sh): append PATHS a mechanical regeneration overwrites, and deliberately exclude CONTENT obligations (a lint-suppression allowlist entry, an identifier rename, a suppression-reason comment, a per-ledger-row doc-comment requirement) even when they are forced by the same triggering edit, because the required content cannot be computed from a plan's declared paths alone -- it would require running the actual lint/naming/ledger check. Reusable test when deciding whether to widen any similar append-only mechanical stage: can the exact content be derived from the declared paths alone, or does deriving it require running the check itself?

sapience_notes.subject: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh generated-surface appending
sapience_notes.value: The stage correctly computes and appends both claimed-missed surfaces (a root README.md generated-inventory block and typst/generated/status.typ) for the cited BimodalLogic module-wiring incident; both offered hypotheses for why it allegedly missed them (no .lean path harvested; ancestor-chain walk stopping short of repo root) were falsified by direct reproduction against the live checkout.

sapience_notes.subject: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh scope ruling
sapience_notes.value: Ruled NO on widening the generated-surface append to cover content obligations (lint-suppression allowlist entries, identifier renames, suppression-reason comments, per-ledger-row doc-comment requirements), because the stage appends PATHS a mechanical regeneration overwrites, while those four are CONTENT obligations whose required content is not computable from a plan's declared paths without running the lint/naming/ledger check itself.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh file_scope visibility
sapience_notes.value: The implement-dispatch prompt composer does not read the dispatching task's own file_scope -- confirmed by grep: exactly one file_scope reference in the whole script, a sibling-batch comment. A surface correctly appended into a task's file_scope is therefore not itself a mid-phase cue to an implementer, so a commit-time gate collision can still occur even when the generated-surface stage works exactly as designed.

sapience_notes.subject: plan-postflight file_scope persistence
sapience_notes.value: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh's harvested array is fed as --file-scope-add into update-task-status.sh postflight for operation_type=plan, persisting the merged array into specs/state.json's file_scope at the [PLANNING] -> [PLANNED] transition. Confirmed by reading orchestrator-postflight.sh's Stage 7 fsa_args construction.

sapience_notes.subject: Bash tool auto-backgrounding
sapience_notes.value: A foreground Bash call wrapped in an inner `timeout N` shell command still gets auto-backgrounded by the harness if it runs past the harness's own default ~120s ceiling; the inner timeout does not raise the harness's own limit. The Bash tool call's own `timeout` parameter (up to 600000ms) must be raised explicitly to avoid this for a genuinely long local command.
